sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ prahṛṣṭo; nanāda coccai rudhirārdragātraḥ nanarta caivātibalo mahātmā; vṛtraṃ nihatyeva sahasranetraḥ
english: Having spoken these words, exultant and his limbs drenched with blood, he roared aloud; and that mighty-souled hero of surpassing strength danced, even as the Thousand-eyed One had danced after slaying Vṛtra.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca duḥśāsane tu nihate putrās tava mahārathāḥ mahākrodhaviṣā vīrāḥ samareṣv apalāyinaḥ daśa rājan mahāvīryo bhīmaṃ prācchādayañ śaraiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When Duḥśāsana had been slain, ten of your sons, great chariot-warriors, heroes venomous with mighty wrath and never fleeing in battle, men of vast valor, O king, covered Bhīma over with their arrows.

sanskrit: kavacī niṣaṅgī pāśī daṇḍadhāro dhanurdharaḥ alolupaḥ śalaḥ saṃdho vātavegasuvarcasau
english: They were Kavacin, Niṣaṅgin, Pāśin, Daṇḍadhāra, Dhanurdhara, Alolupa, Śala, Saṃdha, Vātavega, and Suvarcas.

sanskrit: ete sametya sahitā bhrātṛvyasanakarśitāḥ bhīmasenaṃ mahābāhuṃ mārgaṇaiḥ samavārayan
english: These, gathered together and grieved by the calamity that had befallen their brother, hemmed in with their arrows the mighty-armed Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: sa vāryamāṇo viśikhaiḥ samantāt tair mahārathaiḥ bhīmaḥ krodhābhiraktākṣaḥ kruddhaḥ kāla ivābabhau
english: Hemmed in on every side by the arrows of those great chariot-warriors, Bhīma, his eyes reddened with anger and full of wrath, shone like Death himself.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu bhallair mahāvegair daśabhir daśabhiḥ śitaiḥ rukmāṅgado rukmapuṅkhaiḥ pārtho ninye yamakṣayam
english: But the son of Pṛthā, his armlets of gold, with ten swift, keen broad-headed shafts feathered with gold, sent them, every one, to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: hateṣu teṣu vīreṣu pradudrāva balaṃ tava paśyataḥ sūtaputrasya pāṇḍavasya bhayārditam
english: When those heroes had been slain, your host, tormented with fear, fled before the Pāṇḍava, even as the Sūta's son looked on.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo mahārāja praviveśa mahāraṇam dṛṣṭvā bhīmasya vikrāntam antakasya prajāsv iva
english: Then, O great king, Karṇa entered into the mighty fray, having beheld the prowess of Bhīma, which was like that of the Destroyer among living creatures.

sanskrit: tasya tv ākārabhāvajñaḥ śalyaḥ samitiśobhanaḥ uvāca vacanaṃ karṇaṃ prāptakālam ariṃdama mā vyathāṃ kuru rādheya naitat tvayy upapadyate
english: But Śalya, splendid in assembly and knowing his bearing and his mood, spoke to Karṇa words fitting to the hour, O tamer of foes: "Yield not to dismay, O son of Rādhā; this becomes you not."

sanskrit: ete dravanti rājāno bhīmasenabhayārditāḥ duryodhanaś ca saṃmūḍho bhrātṛvyasanaduḥkhitaḥ
english: "These kings are fleeing, tormented by fear of Bhīmasena, and Duryodhana too is stupefied, stricken with grief at the destruction of his brothers."

sanskrit: duḥśāsanasya rudhire pīyamāne mahātmanā vyāpannacetasaś caiva śokopahatamanyavaḥ
english: "While Duḥśāsana's blood was being drunk by that great-souled one, their senses failed them and their spirits were broken by grief."

sanskrit: duryodhanam upāsante parivārya samantataḥ kṛpaprabhṛtayaḥ karṇa hataśeṣāś ca sodarāḥ
english: "Surrounding him on every side, O Karṇa, Kṛpa and the rest, together with the brothers who survived the slaughter, wait upon Duryodhana."

sanskrit: pāṇḍavā labdhalakṣāś ca dhanaṃjayapurogamāḥ tvām evābhimukhāḥ śūrā yuddhāya samupāsthitāḥ
english: "And the Pāṇḍavas, sure of their aim and led by Dhanaṃjaya, those heroes, have come forward facing you alone, ready for battle."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla pauruṣe mahati sthitaḥ kṣatradharmaṃ puraskṛtya pratyudyāhi dhanaṃjayam
english: "Therefore, O tiger among men, standing firm in your great manhood and setting the warrior's duty foremost, go forth to meet Dhanaṃjaya."

sanskrit: bhāro hi dhārtarāṣṭreṇa tvayi sarvaḥ samarpitaḥ tam udvaha mahābāho yathāśakti yathābalam jaye syād vipulā kīrtir dhruvaḥ svargaḥ parājaye
english: "For the whole burden has been laid upon you by Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son; bear it up, O mighty-armed one, according to your power and your strength. In victory there will be abundant glory, and in defeat heaven is assured."

sanskrit: vṛṣasenaś ca rādheya saṃkruddhas tanayas tava tvayi mohasamāpanne pāṇḍavān abhidhāvati
english: "And while you are sunk in bewilderment, O son of Rādhā, your enraged son Vṛṣasena is rushing upon the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ śalyasyāmitatejasaḥ hṛdi mānuṣyakaṃ bhāvaṃ cakre yuddhāya susthiram
english: Having heard this speech of Śalya of measureless splendor, he steadied his human spirit firmly in his heart for the battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho vṛṣaseno 'bhyadhāvad; ātasthivāṃsaṃ svarathaṃ hatārim vṛkodaraṃ kālam ivāttadaṇḍaṃ; gadāhastaṃ pothamānaṃ tvadīyān
english: Then the enraged Vṛṣasena rushed against Vṛkodara—who had slain his foe and mounted his own chariot, mace in hand like Death wielding his rod—as he was crushing your warriors.

sanskrit: tam abhyadhāvan nakulaḥ pravīro; roṣād amitraṃ pratudan pṛṣatkaiḥ karṇasya putraṃ samare prahṛṣṭaṃ; jiṣṇur jighāṃsur maghaveva jambham
english: Against him the foremost hero Nakula rushed, in his fury piercing the foe with his shafts—against Karṇa's son, exultant in the fray—the victorious one eager to slay him, as Maghavan once sought to slay Jambha.

sanskrit: tato dhvajaṃ sphāṭikacitrakambuṃ; ciccheda vīro nakulaḥ kṣureṇa karṇātmajasyeṣvasanaṃ ca citraṃ; bhallena jāmbūnadapaṭṭanaddham
english: Then the hero Nakula with a razor-edged shaft cut down the banner, bright with crystal and conch-shell, and with a broad-headed arrow shattered Karṇa's son's gleaming bow, bound with bands of pure gold.

sanskrit: athānyad ādāya dhanuḥ suśīghraṃ; karṇātmajaḥ pāṇḍavam abhyavidhyat divyair mahāstrair nakulaṃ mahāstro; duḥśāsanasyāpacitiṃ yiyāsuḥ
english: Then Karṇa's son, taking up another bow with great speed, pierced the Pāṇḍava; that master of mighty weapons struck Nakula with celestial great weapons, seeking to avenge Duḥśāsana.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho nakulas taṃ mahātmā; śarair maholkāpratimair avidhyat divyair astrair abhyavidhyac ca so 'pi; karṇasya putro nakulaṃ kṛtāstraḥ
english: Then the enraged, great-souled Nakula pierced him with arrows like great meteors; and Karṇa's son too, skilled in arms, pierced Nakula in return with celestial weapons.

sanskrit: karṇasya putro nakulasya rājan; sarvān aśvān akṣiṇod uttamāstraiḥ vanāyujān sukumārasya śubhrān; alaṃkṛtāñ jātarūpeṇa śīghrān
english: Karṇa's son, O king, with his choicest weapons destroyed all the horses of the delicate Nakula—horses of the Vanāyu breed, white and swift, adorned with gold.

sanskrit: tato hatāśvād avaruhya yānād; ādāya carma ruciraṃ cāṣṭacandram ākāśasaṃkāśam asiṃ gṛhītvā; poplūyamānaḥ khagavac cacāra
english: Then, alighting from his car whose horses were slain, he took up a beautiful shield marked with eight moons and, grasping a sword the color of the sky, he ranged about, leaping like a bird.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣe nṛvarāśvanāgāṃś; ciccheda mārgān vicaran vicitrān te prāpatann asinā gāṃ viśastā; yathāśvamedhe paśavaḥ śamitrā
english: Then, coursing aloft through the air in wondrous paths, he cut down foremost men and horses and elephants; slain by his sword, they fell to the earth, like beasts slaughtered by the immolators at a horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit: dvisāhasrā viditā yuddhaśauṇḍā; nānādeśyāḥ subhṛtāḥ satyasaṃdhāḥ ekena śīghraṃ nakulena kṛttāḥ; sārepsunevottamacandanās te
english: Two thousand renowned warriors, valiant in battle, from many lands, well-nourished and true to their pledges, were swiftly cut down by Nakula alone, as fine sandalwood trees are felled by one who craves their essence.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ nakulaṃ so 'bhipatya; samantataḥ sāyakair abhyavidhyat sa tudyamāno nakulaḥ pṛṣatkair; vivyādha vīraṃ sa cukopa viddhaḥ
english: As Nakula came on, he too fell upon him and pierced him on every side with his shafts; and Nakula, thus stung with arrows, pierced the hero in return, who, wounded, was filled with wrath.

sanskrit: taṃ karṇaputro vidhamantam ekaṃ; narāśvamātaṅgarathapravekān krīḍantam aṣṭādaśabhiḥ pṛṣatkair; vivyādha vīraṃ sa cukopa viddhaḥ
english: As he, single-handed, scattered the foremost of men, horses, elephants, and chariots, sporting as he went, Karṇa's son pierced that hero with eighteen shafts; and he, wounded, was filled with wrath.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyadhāvat samare jighāṃsuḥ; karṇātmajaṃ pāṇḍusuto nṛvīraḥ tasyeṣubhir vyadhamat karṇaputro; mahāraṇe carma sahasratāram
english: Then the heroic son of Pāṇḍu rushed in the fray, eager to slay Karṇa's son; but Karṇa's son with his arrows shattered, in that great battle, his shield studded with a thousand stars.

sanskrit: tasyāyasaṃ niśitaṃ tīkṣṇadhāram; asiṃ vikośaṃ gurubhārasāham dviṣaccharīrāpaharaṃ sughoram; ādhunvataḥ sarpam ivograrūpam
english: As he brandished his iron sword, whetted and keen-edged, unsheathed, able to bear a heavy stroke, the bearer-away of foemen's bodies, most terrible, dreadful in form like a serpent—

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ śaraiḥ ṣaḍbhir amitrasāhaś; cakarta khaḍgaṃ niśitaiḥ sudhāraiḥ punaś ca pītair niśitaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ; stanāntare gāḍham athābhyavidhyat
english: —that subduer of foes swiftly, with six keen, well-edged arrows, cut the sword in two, and again with sharp, whetted shafts, oil-treated, pierced him deep between the breasts.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenasya rathaṃ hatāśvo; mādrīsutaḥ karṇasutābhitaptaḥ āpupluve siṃha ivācalāgraṃ; saṃprekṣamāṇasya dhanaṃjayasya
english: Then Mādrī's son, his horses slain and sore beset by Karṇa's son, leapt up onto Bhīmasena's chariot, like a lion onto a mountain-peak, while Dhanaṃjaya looked on.

sanskrit: nakulam atha viditvā chinnabāṇāsanāsiṃ; viratham ariśarārtaṃ karṇaputrāstrabhagnam pavanadhutapatākā hrādino valgitāśvā; varapuruṣaniyattās te rathāḥ śīghram īyuḥ
english: Then, learning that Nakula's bow and sword were severed, his car destroyed, himself tormented by the foe's arrows and broken by Karṇa's son's weapons, those chariots—banners shaken by the wind, rumbling, horses prancing, driven by the best of men—swiftly came on.

sanskrit: drupadasutavariṣṭhāḥ pañca śaineyaṣaṣṭhā; drupadaduhitṛputrāḥ pañca cāmitrasāhāḥ dviradarathanarāśvān sūdayantas tvadīyān; bhujagapatinikāśair mārgaṇair āttaśastrāḥ
english: The five foremost sons of Drupada, with Śini's grandson as the sixth, and the five sons of Drupada's daughter, subduers of foes, slaying your elephants, chariots, men, and horses with arrows like serpent-lords, came on with weapons in hand.

sanskrit: atha tava rathamukhyās tān pratīyus tvaranto; hṛdikasutakṛpau ca drauṇiduryodhanau ca śakuniśukavṛkāś ca krāthadevāvṛdhau ca; dviradajaladaghoṣaiḥ syandanaiḥ kārmukaiś ca
english: Then your foremost chariot-warriors went forth against them in haste—Hṛdika's son and Kṛpa, Droṇa's son and Duryodhana, Śakuni, Śuka, and Vṛka, and Krātha and Devāvṛdha—with chariots that thundered like elephants and rain-clouds, and with their bows.

sanskrit: tava naravaravaryās tān daśaikaṃ ca vīrān; pravaraśaravarāgryais tāḍayanto 'bhyarundhan navajaladasavarṇair hastibhis tān udīyur; giriśikharanikāśair bhīmavegaiḥ kuṇindāḥ
english: Your foremost of warriors, smiting those eleven heroes with their choicest excellent shafts, hemmed them in; but the Kuṇindas rode up against them on elephants the hue of fresh rain-clouds, like mountain-peaks and of terrible speed.

sanskrit: sukalpitā haimavatā madotkaṭā; raṇābhikāmaiḥ kṛtibhiḥ samāsthitāḥ suvarṇajālāvatatā babhur gajās; tathā yathā vai jaladāḥ savidyutaḥ
english: Well-caparisoned, born of the Himālaya, furious with rut, mounted by skilled men eager for battle, those elephants overspread with nets of gold shone forth like rain-clouds charged with lightning.

sanskrit: kuṇindaputro daśabhir mahāyasaiḥ; kṛpaṃ sasūtāśvam apīḍayad bhṛśam tataḥ śaradvatsutasāyakair hataḥ; sahaiva nāgena papāta bhūtale
english: The son of the Kuṇinda king with ten great iron shafts sorely afflicted Kṛpa together with his charioteer and horses; but slain by the arrows of Śaradvat's son, he fell to the ground along with his elephant.

sanskrit: kuṇindaputrāvarajas tu tomarair; divākarāṃśupratimair ayasmayaiḥ rathaṃ ca vikṣobhya nanāda nardatas; tato 'sya gāndhārapatiḥ śiro 'harat
english: But the younger brother of the Kuṇinda's son, with iron lances like the rays of the sun, shook a chariot and roared aloud; thereupon the lord of the Gāndhāras struck off his head as he roared.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuṇindeṣu hateṣu teṣv atha; prahṛṣṭarūpās tava te mahārathāḥ bhṛśaṃ pradadhmur lavaṇāmbusaṃbhavān; parāṃś ca bāṇāsanapāṇayo 'bhyayuḥ
english: Then, when those Kuṇindas had been slain, your great chariot-warriors, exultant in look, loudly blew their conches born of the salt sea, and, bows in hand, advanced against the foe.

sanskrit: athābhavad yuddham atīva dāruṇaṃ; punaḥ kurūṇāṃ saha pāṇḍusṛñjayaiḥ śarāsiśaktyṛṣṭigadāparaśvadhair; narāśvanāgāsuharaṃ bhṛśākulam
english: Then there arose once more a most terrible battle between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas—with arrows, swords, spears, lances, maces, and battle-axes—a fearfully turbulent fray that bore off the life-breath of men and horses and elephants.

sanskrit: rathāśvamātaṅgapadātibhis tataḥ; parasparaṃ viprahatāpatan kṣitau yathā savidyutstanitā balāhakāḥ; samāsthitā digbhya ivogramārutaiḥ
english: Then chariots, horses, elephants, and foot-soldiers, striking one another, fell to the earth, like clouds charged with lightning and thunder driven together from the quarters by fierce winds.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatānīkahatān mahāgajāṃs; tathā rathān pattigaṇāṃś ca tāvakān jaghāna bhojaś ca hayān athāpatan; viśastrakṛttāḥ kṛtavarmaṇā dvipāḥ
english: Then Śatānīka slew your great elephants, your chariots, and your troops of foot-soldiers; and the Bhoja chief slew the horses; and the elephants, cut down and disarmed by Kṛtavarman, fell.

sanskrit: athāpare drauṇiśarāhatā dvipās; trayaḥ sasarvāyudhayodhaketavaḥ nipetur urvyāṃ vyasavaḥ prapātitās; tathā yathā vajrahatā mahācalāḥ
english: Then three other elephants, struck by the arrows of Droṇa's son, with all their weapons, warriors, and standards, fell lifeless to the earth, hurled down like great mountains smitten by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: kuṇindarājāvarajād anantaraḥ; stanāntare patrivarair atāḍayat tavātmajaṃ tasya tavātmajaḥ śaraiḥ; śitaiḥ śarīraṃ bibhide dvipaṃ ca tam
english: He who was next after the younger brother of the Kuṇinda king smote your son between the breasts with excellent feathered shafts; but your son with his keen arrows pierced his body and his elephant.

sanskrit: sa nāgarājaḥ saha rājasūnunā; papāta raktaṃ bahu sarvataḥ kṣaran śacīśavajraprahato 'mbudāgame; yathā jalaṃ gairikaparvatas tathā
english: That lord of elephants, together with the prince, fell, pouring forth much blood on every side, as a mountain of red ochre, struck by the thunderbolt of Śacī's lord, pours down its waters at the coming of the clouds.

sanskrit: kuṇindaputraprahito 'paradvipaḥ; śukaṃ sasūtāśvarathaṃ vyapothayat tato 'patat krāthaśarābhidāritaḥ; saheśvaro vajrahato yathā giriḥ
english: Another elephant, urged on by the Kuṇinda's son, crushed Śuka together with his charioteer, horses, and car; then, torn by Krātha's arrows, it fell along with its rider, like a mountain smitten by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: rathī dvipasthena hato 'patac charaiḥ; krāthādhipaḥ parvatajena durjayaḥ savājisūteṣvasanas tathāpatad; yathā mahāvātahato mahādrumaḥ
english: The chariot-warrior Krātha, the unconquerable lord, was struck by the arrows of the mountain-born one mounted on his elephant and fell, together with his horses, charioteer, and bow, like a great tree felled by a mighty wind.

sanskrit: vṛko dvipasthaṃ girirājavāsinaṃ; bhṛśaṃ śarair dvādaśabhiḥ parābhinat tato vṛkaṃ sāśvarathaṃ mahājavaṃ; tvaraṃś caturbhiś caraṇe vyapothayat
english: Vṛka sorely pierced with twelve arrows the dweller of the great mountains who rode his elephant; thereupon that one in haste with four shafts crushed swift-moving Vṛka, together with his horses and car, at the feet.

sanskrit: sa nāgarājaḥ saniyantṛko 'patat; parāhato babhrusuteṣubhir bhṛśam sa cāpi devāvṛdhasūnur arditaḥ; papāta nunnaḥ sahadevasūnunā
english: That lord of elephants, together with its driver, fell, sorely smitten by the arrows of Babhru's son; and Devāvṛdha's son too, afflicted and struck down by Sahadeva's son, fell.

sanskrit: viṣāṇapotrāparagātraghātinā; gajena hantuṃ śakuneḥ kuṇindajaḥ jagāma vegena bhṛśārdayaṃś ca taṃ; tato 'sya gāndhārapatiḥ śiro 'harat
english: On an elephant whose tusks, trunk, and other limbs were slayers of foes, the Kuṇinda's son went with speed to slay Śakuni, sorely afflicting him; thereupon the lord of the Gāndhāras struck off his head.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatānīkahatā mahāgajā; hayā rathāḥ pattigaṇāś ca tāvakāḥ suparṇavātaprahatā yathā nagās; tathā gatā gām avaśā vicūrṇitāḥ
english: Then your great elephants, horses, chariots, and bands of foot-soldiers, slain by Śatānīka, like trees struck by the wind of Garuḍa's wings, went helplessly to the earth, crushed to powder.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyavidhyad bahubhiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ; kuṇindaputro nakulātmajaṃ smayan tato 'sya kāyān nicakarta nākuliḥ; śiraḥ kṣureṇāmbujasaṃnibhānanam
english: Then the Kuṇinda's son, smiling, pierced Nakula's son with many keen arrows; thereupon Nakula's son with a razor-edged shaft severed from his body his head, whose face was like a lotus.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatānīkam avidhyad āśugais; tribhiḥ śitaiḥ karṇasuto 'rjunaṃ tribhiḥ tribhiś ca bhīmaṃ nakulaṃ ca saptabhir; janārdanaṃ dvādaśabhiś ca sāyakaiḥ
english: Then Karṇa's son pierced Śatānīka with three swift keen shafts, Arjuna with three, Bhīma with three, Nakula with seven, and Janārdana with twelve arrows.

sanskrit: tad asya karmātimanuṣyakarmaṇaḥ; samīkṣya hṛṣṭāḥ kuravo 'bhyapūjayan parākramajñās tu dhanaṃjayasya te; huto 'yam agnāv iti taṃ tu menire
english: Beholding that deed of his, surpassing the deeds of men, the Kurus, rejoicing, applauded him; yet those who knew Dhanaṃjaya's prowess deemed him already as an oblation cast into the fire.

sanskrit: tataḥ kirīṭī paravīraghātī; hatāśvam ālokya narapravīram tam abhyadhāvad vṛṣasenam āhave; sa sūtajasya pramukhe sthitaṃ tadā
english: Then the Diademed One, slayer of hostile heroes, beholding that foremost of men, Vṛṣasena, whose horses had been slain, rushed against him in battle, as he stood then before the Sūta's son.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ naravīram ugraṃ; mahāhave bāṇasahasradhāriṇam abhyāpatat karṇasuto mahāratho; yathaiva cendraṃ namuciḥ purātane
english: As that fierce hero among men came on in the great battle, bearing a thousand arrows, Karṇa's son, the great chariot-warrior, fell upon him, even as Namuci fell upon Indra in the days of old.

sanskrit: tato 'dbhutenaikaśatena pārthaṃ; śarair viddhvā sūtaputrasya putraḥ nanāda nādaṃ sumahānubhāvo; viddhveva śakraṃ namuciḥ purā vai
english: Then, having pierced the son of Pṛthā with a wondrous hundred arrows, the Sūta's son's son, of great might, roared aloud, as Namuci of old roared when he had pierced Śakra.

sanskrit: punaḥ sa pārthaṃ vṛṣasena ugrair; bāṇair avidhyad bhujamūlamadhye tathaiva kṛṣṇaṃ navabhiḥ samārdayat; punaś ca pārthaṃ daśabhiḥ śitāgraiḥ
english: Again Vṛṣasena pierced the son of Pṛthā with fierce arrows in the joints of the shoulders, and likewise afflicted Kṛṣṇa with nine, and again the son of Pṛthā with ten keen-pointed shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ kirīṭī raṇamūrdhni kopāt; kṛtvā triśākhāṃ bhrukuṭiṃ lalāṭe mumoca bāṇān viśikhān mahātmā; vadhāya rājan sūtaputrasya saṃkhye
english: Then the Diademed One, at the head of the battle, knitting in his wrath a three-forked frown upon his brow, the great-souled one loosed his keen arrows, O king, to slay the Sūta's son in the fray.

sanskrit: vivyādha cainaṃ daśabhiḥ pṛṣatkair; marmasv asaktaṃ prasabhaṃ kirīṭī ciccheda cāsyeṣvasanaṃ bhujau ca; kṣuraiś caturbhiḥ śira eva cograiḥ
english: And the Diademed One pierced him forcibly with ten shafts in his vital parts where he was unguarded, and with four razor-edged arrows, fierce ones, cut off his bow, his arms, and his very head.

sanskrit: sa pārthabāṇābhihataḥ papāta; rathād vibāhur viśirā dharāyām supuṣpitaḥ parṇadharo 'tikāyo; vāteritaḥ śāla ivādriśṛṅgāt
english: Struck by the arrows of Pṛthā's son, he fell from his chariot to the earth, armless and headless, his huge frame like a fair-blossomed, leaf-laden sāla tree shaken by the wind from a mountain-crest.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣya bāṇābhihataṃ patantaṃ; rathāt sutaṃ sūtajaḥ kṣiprakārī rathaṃ rathenāśu jagāma vegāt; kirīṭinaḥ putravadhābhitaptaḥ
english: Beholding his son, struck by the arrows, falling from the chariot, the swift-acting son of the Sūta, sorely pained by his son's slaying, swiftly drove his car with speed against the chariot of the Diademed One.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vṛṣasenaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā śokāmarṣasamanvitaḥ muktvā śokodbhavaṃ vāri netrābhyāṃ sahasā vṛṣaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding Vṛṣasena slain, the Bull among men, filled with grief and indignation, suddenly let fall from his eyes the waters born of sorrow.

sanskrit: rathena karṇas tejasvī jagāmābhimukho ripūn yuddhāyāmarṣatāmrākṣaḥ samāhūya dhanaṃjayam
english: Karṇa the splendid drove his chariot straight against the foe, his eyes coppery-red with wrath, challenging Dhanaṃjaya to battle.

sanskrit: tau rathau sūryasaṃkāśau vaiyāghraparivāraṇau sametau dadṛśus tatra dvāv ivārkau samāgatau
english: Those two chariots, bright as the sun and draped with tiger-skins, men saw come together there like two suns met in one place.

sanskrit: śvetāśvau puruṣādityāv āsthitāv arimardanau śuśubhāte mahātmānau candrādityau yathā divi
english: Borne by white horses, those two suns among men, those crushers of foes, those great-souled ones, shone as they stood, like the moon and the sun in the sky.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā vismayaṃ jagmuḥ sarvabhūtāni māriṣa trailokyavijaye yattāv indravairocanāv iva
english: Beholding the two, all beings fell into wonder, O sir, as though they were Indra and the son of Virocana striving for the conquest of the three worlds.

sanskrit: rathajyātalanirhrādair bāṇaśaṅkharavair api tau rathāv abhidhāvantau samālokya mahīkṣitām
english: With the din of chariots, bowstrings, and leather guards, and with the clamor of arrows and conches, those two chariots rushed onward, while the lords of earth looked on.

sanskrit: dhvajau ca dṛṣṭvā saṃsaktau vismayaḥ samapadyata hastikakṣyāṃ ca karṇasya vānaraṃ ca kirīṭinaḥ
english: And seeing the two standards joined in close conflict—Karṇa's elephant-girth emblem and the ape of the Diademed One—wonder arose in them.

sanskrit: tau rathau saṃprasaktau ca dṛṣṭvā bhārata pārthivāḥ siṃhanādaravāṃś cakruḥ sādhuvādāṃś ca puṣkalān
english: And seeing those two chariots locked together, O Bhārata, the kings raised lion-roars and abundant cries of applause.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu dvairathaṃ tābhyāṃ tatra yodhāḥ samantataḥ cakrur bāhuvalaṃ caiva tathā celavalaṃ mahat
english: And hearing of the single combat between the two, the warriors on every side raised a great clamor of beating arms and waving garments.

sanskrit: ājagmuḥ kuravas tatra vāditrānugatās tadā karṇaṃ praharṣayantaś ca śaṅkhān dadhmuś ca puṣkalān
english: The Kurus came thither then, accompanied by music, and, gladdening Karṇa, blew their conches in abundance.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ sarve harṣayanto dhanaṃjayam tūryaśaṅkhaninādena diśaḥ sarvā vyanādayan
english: Likewise all the Pāṇḍavas, gladdening Dhanaṃjaya, made all the quarters resound with the blare of trumpets and conches.

sanskrit: kṣveḍitāsphoṭitotkruṣṭais tumulaṃ sarvato 'bhavat bāhughoṣāś ca vīrāṇāṃ karṇārjunasamāgame
english: With roars, the slapping of arms, and shouts, there was tumult on every side, and the din of warriors' arms at the meeting of Karṇa and Arjuna.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā puruṣavyāghrau rathasthau rathināṃ varau pragṛhītamahācāpau śaraśaktigadāyudhau
english: Beholding those two tigers among men, foremost of chariot-warriors, standing upon their cars, their great bows grasped, armed with arrows, spears, and maces—

sanskrit: varmiṇau baddhanistriṃśau śvetāśvau śaṅkhaśobhinau tūṇīravarasaṃpannau dvāv api sma sudarśanau
english: —clad in mail, swords girded on, borne by white horses, splendid with conches, furnished with excellent quivers, the two of them were fair to behold.

sanskrit: raktacandanadigdhāṅgau samadau vṛṣabhāv iva āśīviṣasamaprakhyau yamakālāntakopamau
english: Their limbs smeared with red sandal-paste, like two bulls in rut, resembling venomous serpents, like Yama, Time, and the Destroyer—

sanskrit: indravṛtrāv iva kruddhau sūryācandramasaprabhau mahāgrahāv iva krūrau yugānte samupasthitau
english: —wrathful like Indra and Vṛtra, radiant as the sun and moon, fierce as two great planets risen at the ending of an age—

sanskrit: devagarbhau devasamau devatulyau ca rūpataḥ sametau puruṣavyāghrau prekṣya karṇadhanaṃjayau
english: —divinely born, godlike, equal to the gods in form—beholding those two tigers among men, Karṇa and Dhanaṃjaya, come together.
